disclosure_text: I am originally from an African country and moved to Canada 10 years ago. So, the issue of being an immigrant has been part of me and an identity that I seem to carry almost each day of my life. Also, because of the smaller number of the people who look like me or whom I share same cultural background makes bare the identity of being a minority.
micronarrative:
This feels somewhat distant because I am not an undocumented or illegal migrant. However, I feel it can affect me if some random person in the crowd walks and asks to know whether I am in the country legally or not. 

Well, I was on a bus going home after work, and the person sitting beside me started a conversation. I jumped into it, but in the middle of the conversation, out of nowhere, he asked, "So, how did you come to Canada?" It felt annoying that a random guy could ask me that. I answered briefly, saying that I came here as a student and then got a job. I then pretended I was having a phone call and alighted at the next bus stop.

Depends on the situation. I totally avoid situations where conversations can get tense and aggressive. I would try to de-escalate as much as possible and walk away. The one that I remember was when I went out with my friends to enjoy a live band. On our way home later that evening, we met a group of people, and one of them verbally abused my friend. My friend was angry and very furious, ready to react. I talked him down, and he listened. It’s moments like these that remind me of the importance of staying calm and understanding, even when things get heated.
